narrativeReportMd:
# EnrollmentRequest R4→R6 breaking-change assessment

## Bottom line
No local R4-valid `EnrollmentRequest` instance pattern was found that becomes invalid solely because of the local R6 `EnrollmentRequest` definition. The material local change is a widening of `EnrollmentRequest.candidate` from `Reference(Patient)` to `Reference(Patient | Group)`, which creates a high R6-to-R4 representability gap and can affect generated clients or validators that still assume the candidate is always a Patient.

## Scope
The comparison used the local R4 and R6 core StructureDefinitions, package indexes, package metadata, and the `fm-status` ValueSet/CodeSystem artifacts. Inherited `Resource`/`DomainResource` changes visible in snapshots were not reported as local findings.

## Main migration themes
R4→R6 migration is mostly additive for this resource: local element names, cardinalities, local non-reference types, and the status code set are stable. R6→R4 or mixed-version exchange needs attention when R6 senders use a Group candidate, because the JSON reference shape can be serialized but is outside the R4 target-profile contract.

## Highest-impact findings
The only material local finding is `EnrollmentRequest:REFERENCE_TARGET:EnrollmentRequest.candidate:group-added`, covering the new Group target on `candidate`.

## Findings requiring human review
Group enrollment backports require business review because a Group candidate cannot be losslessly reduced to a single Patient candidate without changing the enrollment subject semantics.

## Backward-compatible design observations
The R6 change is additive and likely intended to represent enrollment for a group of subjects. It was backward-compatible for R4 instances moving forward, but not for R6 data sent back to strict R4 systems.

## Follow-up analysis
Base `Resource` and `DomainResource` reports should own inherited snapshot-level changes. Profiles and implementation guides should be reviewed separately if a deployment constrains EnrollmentRequest candidate handling.

summary.executiveSummaryMd: No hard local R4→R6 validation break was found for `EnrollmentRequest`. The main concern is that R6 allows `EnrollmentRequest.candidate` to reference `Group`, while R4 allowed only `Patient`; the top uncertainty is the absence of an official narrative diff explaining intended migration semantics.
summary.migrationThemesMd: Forward migration is low friction for existing base R4 instances because local elements and cardinalities are preserved and the required `status` code set is unchanged. Mixed R4/R6 exchange is riskier: R6 Group candidates need explicit handling for R4 validators, R4 generated models, reporting logic, and business workflows that previously treated enrollment candidate as a single patient.
summary.confidenceSummaryMd: Confidence is high for the computable delta because both assigned StructureDefinitions exist under the same canonical URL and the local element diff is small. Confidence in rationale and real-world prevalence is medium because official change notes, rendered narrative pages, and deployment profiles were not available in the local inputs.

oldState.narrativeMd: In R4, `EnrollmentRequest.candidate` was optional but, when present, its target profile was limited to `Patient`. The local definition text also described the value as a patient resource.

newState.narrativeMd: In R6 ballot4, the same optional element remains a `Reference`, but the allowed target profiles are broadened to include `Group`. The short and definition text were updated to describe a subject or group of subjects.

facts.note: The local semantics were broadened to match the added target.

structuredDelta.matchingRationaleMd: The element id and path are unchanged across R4 and R6, so this is a same-element target-domain widening rather than a rename or move.

impact.impactRationaleMd: Existing R4 instances with absent `candidate` or a Patient candidate remain valid against the local R6 resource definition. The breaking mechanism is reverse-direction and mixed-version: a valid R6 instance can now contain `candidate.reference = "Group/..."`, which a strict R4 validator should reject because R4 targetProfile permits only Patient. Generated R4 clients that expose typed `Reference<Patient>` accessors or business logic that dereferences candidate as a Patient can fail or silently mis-handle the enrollment subject.
impact.safetyOrBusinessRiskMd: Dropping or mis-converting a Group candidate can change who is being enrolled, producing payer/business workflow errors even though the resource is not directly clinical.

justification.inferredGoal: Allow enrollment requests for a group of subjects rather than only a single patient.
justification.backwardCompatibleAlternativeSummary: This is not a breaking R4-to-R6 base-design issue: every R4-valid Patient candidate remains allowed in R6, and the added Group target only creates R6-to-R4 representability risk.
justification.justificationRationaleMd: The inferred goal--allowing enrollment requests for a group of subjects--is reasonable and is directly reflected in the R6 target-profile widening plus updated `candidate` definition. Because the base R6 change preserves existing R4-valid `EnrollmentRequest.candidate` instances, the level of R4-to-R6 breakage is effectively none; the remaining concern is reverse-direction compatibility when R6 Group candidates are sent to R4 systems.
justification.backwardCompatibleAlternativeMd: No backward-compatible base-design alternative is applicable for the R4-to-R6 direction, because the R6 design already preserves the R4 Patient-only target as a subset. Keeping Group support out of the base resource and using an extension or profile could ease R6-to-R4 exchange, but that would be a mitigation for older receivers and would weaken uniform core validation and discoverability of group enrollment in R6.
justification.alternativeTradeoffSummary: Extension or profile-based handling can mitigate exchange with R4 systems, but it is a down-conversion/backport strategy rather than a less-breaking R6 base design.

findings.narrativeMd: `EnrollmentRequest.candidate` is the same element in both versions, but R6 broadens its reference target from Patient-only to Patient-or-Group. This does not invalidate existing R4 EnrollmentRequest instances, because every R4-allowed candidate target remains allowed. It does create a material interoperability hazard when R6 data is consumed by R4 systems or when generated models assumed the candidate is always a Patient.
findings.validationAndCompatibilityMd: An R4-valid instance with a Patient candidate remains locally valid in R6. A new R6 instance with a Group candidate is not cleanly representable as a conformant R4 EnrollmentRequest because R4's targetProfile list excludes Group. Strict validators can reject it; loose JSON parsers may accept the `Reference` shape but later fail target validation or patient-specific dereferencing.
findings.migrationGuidanceMd: R4→R6 transforms do not need to change existing Patient candidates. For R6→R4 exchange, detect `candidate` references whose target resource type is `Group`. There is no lossless base R4 mapping: either retain the semantics through an extension/profile-specific convention, split into patient-specific enrollment requests only when that is business-correct, or reject/quarantine the record for manual review. Tests should include absent candidate, Patient candidate, and Group candidate cases.
findings.backwardCompatibilityAnalysisMd: The change is additive for forward migration and probably reflects a real need for group enrollment. The backward-compatible alternative would have been an extension or profile while keeping the base target Patient-only. That alternative would reduce R4 backport risk but would make Group support less visible and less consistently validated in the R6 core resource.
findings.reviewerNotesMd: Human review is mainly needed for deployment-specific R6→R4 policy, not for identifying the computable delta.

checkedNoMaterialChange.notesMd: The canonical URL, id, name, kind, type, baseDefinition, derivation, and abstract flag are stable. The artifact's publication/status metadata changed and is listed as a non-breaking notable change.
The local element ids are the same in R4 and R6: root, `identifier`, `status`, `created`, `insurer`, `provider`, `candidate`, and `coverage`.
All local cardinalities are unchanged, including `identifier` at `0..*` and all other local data elements at `0..1`.
Local type codes are stable: `Identifier`, `code`, `dateTime`, and `Reference`. The only type-domain change is the `candidate` reference target addition captured as a finding.

`EnrollmentRequest.status` remains a required binding to `http://hl7.org/fhir/ValueSet/fm-status`; the version suffix changes from `4.0.1` to `6.0.0-ballot4`. The ValueSet compose still includes `http://hl7.org/fhir/fm-status`, and the local CodeSystem concepts remain `active`, `cancelled`, `draft`, and `entered-in-error`. No expansion artifacts were present.
No local EnrollmentRequest-specific invariant was added, removed, or changed. Shared `ele-1` and inherited DomainResource constraints are base-artifact matters.
No local fixed value, pattern value, or default value was found in either version.
No local maxLength, regex, minValue, or maxValue constraints were found in either version.
The local `status` element remains a modifier, and other local EnrollmentRequest elements remain non-modifier. Inherited modifier flag behavior is out of scope.
The local `status` element remains `isSummary: true`; other local EnrollmentRequest elements remain not summary. Inherited summary flag changes are out of scope.
No local slicing or slice definitions were present on EnrollmentRequest in either version.

No local element was renamed or changed to a different JSON property shape. The `candidate` target widening can still affect typed generated models even though the serialized `Reference` shape is unchanged.

nonBreakingNotableChanges.title: EnrollmentRequest publication metadata moved from draft/trial-use to active/normative
nonBreakingNotableChanges.whyNotBreakingMd: The canonical identity and instance content model are unchanged by the StructureDefinition `status` and standards-status extension changes. Existing instances do not become invalid because of this publication metadata.
nonBreakingNotableChanges.migrationAwarenessMd: Governance, conformance, or code-generation pipelines that treat normative/active artifacts differently may need to refresh metadata and documentation labels.

nonBreakingNotableChanges.title: Status binding version updated with no observed code-set change
nonBreakingNotableChanges.whyNotBreakingMd: `EnrollmentRequest.status` remains a required binding to `ValueSet/fm-status`. The ValueSet version changes, but the compose system and local CodeSystem concepts are unchanged in the supplied packages.
nonBreakingNotableChanges.migrationAwarenessMd: Validators should use the R6 package for R6 validation. No status-code transform was identified for base EnrollmentRequest instances.

nonBreakingNotableChanges.title: R6 explicitly carries mustSupport false on local elements
nonBreakingNotableChanges.whyNotBreakingMd: R4 omitted `mustSupport` on local elements while R6 explicitly records `false`; in base ElementDefinition semantics, absence is equivalent to not being must-support.
nonBreakingNotableChanges.migrationAwarenessMd: Code that diffs raw JSON should normalize missing boolean defaults before treating this as a semantic change.
